The unanswerable is what makes The Getaway Driver such an interesting piece of theater.
Deborah Salem Smith and Charlie Thurston’s script, incisive staging, and two potent performances turn the evening into a contemporary morality play.
The Getaway Driver has something for everyone.
Otherwise, CST 's "THE GETAWAY DRIVER" is a powerful, impactful story conveyed by two superb actresses.

In “The Getaway Driver,” protesting the Vietnam War lands Katherine Ann Power in a world of trouble. Central Square Theater’s production of the play by Deborah Salem Smith and Charlie Thurston mostly details the life of Power (Rebecca Gibel) and is based on the true story of Power and Clare Schroeder.

cn.t: Critics largely praise *The Getaway Driver* as a morally compelling true-crime drama, with standout performances from its two leads. A few find it uneven, but its unflinching look at political violence and personal guilt resonates.
